lead: A coil turning at constant speed in a uniform magnetic field produces a sinusoidal voltage. This is the basic idea of an AC generator. The mains in India is a 50 Hz sine wave with RMS value 230 V. Peak, average and RMS values describe that wave and let us compare it with steady DC. They are used for meter readings, insulation ratings, rectifier design and power calculations.
prereq: You need: resistance, voltage and current (see Unit 1), plus basic sine, cosine and radians.

sections.h3: A rotating coil gives a sine wave

blocks.text: A coil of N turns and area A rotates at constant angular speed ω in a uniform magnetic field of flux density B. The field passes through the coil at a changing angle. Flux linkage changes as cos ωt, so the induced voltage changes as sin ωt. Slip rings and brushes connect the rotating coil to the outside circuit. The law of induction itself is treated with magnetic circuits in Unit 3, Magnetic Circuits and Electrical Machines.

items: A coil rotates at constant ω in a uniform magnetic field B.
The flux linking the coil is B A cos ωt.
The induced voltage is e = N B A ω sin ωt.
The peak is E<sub>m</sub> = N B A ω; the wave is a sine because the coil turns steadily.

blocks.text: e = E<sub>m</sub> sin ωt = N B A ω sin ωt, with E<sub>m</sub> = N B A ω
blocks.where: e is instantaneous voltage in V; E<sub>m</sub> is peak voltage in V; N is number of turns; B is flux density in T; A is coil area in m²; ω is angular frequency in rad/s; t is time in s.

blocks.text: One complete positive and negative swing is a cycle. The time for one cycle is the period T in s. Frequency f = 1/T in Hz is cycles per second. Angular frequency is ω = 2πf rad/s. In India f = 50 Hz, so T = 20 ms and ω = 314 rad/s.

The instantaneous value is the voltage at one instant t. The peak value V<sub>m</sub> is the largest magnitude. The full-cycle average of a pure sine is zero because the positive and negative halves cancel. The useful average is taken over one half cycle: V<sub>avg</sub> = 2V<sub>m</sub>/π = 0.637V<sub>m</sub>.

blocks.where: V<sub>avg</sub> is half-cycle average voltage in V; V<sub>m</sub> is peak voltage in V; π ≈ 3.1416.

blocks.text: The RMS value is the square root of the mean of the squared wave over one full cycle. For a sine, Vrms = Vm/√2 = 0.707Vm. It is the DC voltage that gives the same heating in a resistor. Some syllabi call it the effective value. The ratio Vrms/Vavg is the form factor; see 2.2.

blocks.where: V<sub>rms</sub> is RMS voltage in V; V<sub>m</sub> is peak voltage in V.

items: Peak value: use for insulation and device voltage ratings. A 230 V RMS mains has 325 V peak.
Half-cycle average: use in rectifier calculations. The full-cycle average of a sine is zero.
RMS: use on AC meters and in power. A 230 V label means 230 V RMS.
The factors 0.637 and 0.707 apply only to a pure sine. For other waveforms use the definitions.

blocks.text: For v = V<sub>m</sub> sin ωt, the wave repeats every 2π radians. At ωt = π/2 the value is V<sub>m</sub>; at ωt = π it is zero; at ωt = 3π/2 it is −V<sub>m</sub>. The meter needle or digital display shows RMS for a sine, not peak. A cheap meter may be calibrated for sine and read wrongly on distorted waves. Meter construction is in Unit 6, Measurements, Power Systems and Electrical Safety.

Power in a resistor is P = Vrms²/R = Irms²R. If you use peak values by mistake, the power comes out twice too large. For a 230 V RMS supply across 100 Ω, P = 230²/100 = 529 W. The peak voltage is 325 V, but 325²/100 is not the average power. Active, reactive and apparent power are covered in 2.5.

blocks.where: P is average power in W; V<sub>rms</sub> and I<sub>rms</sub> are RMS voltage and current; R is resistance in Ω.

figure.caption: A 325 V peak sine wave with horizontal lines at +230 V and −230 V RMS. Notice the RMS line sits at 0.707 of the peak, not at the peak.

spec.aria: Plot of a 325 V peak sine wave with horizontal lines at plus and minus 230 V RMS.

examples.question: A sinusoidal voltage is v = 325 sin(314t) V. Find its peak value, RMS value, half-cycle average value and frequency.
steps: Compare with v = V<sub>m</sub> sin ωt. The peak value is V<sub>m</sub> = 325 V.
The angular frequency is ω = 314 rad/s.
examples.answer: Peak 325 V, RMS 229.8 V (about 230 V), half-cycle average 206.9 V and frequency 50 Hz.
examples.check:
import math
Vm = 325.0
omega = 314.0
Vrms = Vm / math.sqrt(2)
Vavg = 2 * Vm / math.pi
f = omega / (2 * math.pi)
print(round(Vm, 1))
print(round(Vrms, 1))
print(round(Vavg, 1))
print(round(f, 1))

traps: The full-cycle average of a pure sine is zero. If a question asks for average value without saying half cycle, state the half-cycle value and say the full-cycle value is zero.
Peak and RMS are not interchangeable. Use V<sub>m</sub> for insulation or a stated peak; use V<sub>rms</sub> in P = V²/R and meter readings.
ω is in rad/s, not Hz. In v = 325 sin(314t), f = 314/(2π) = 50 Hz, not 314 Hz.
A meter marked AC volts reads RMS for a sine. On a distorted wave, a cheap average-sensing meter can be wrong; a true-RMS meter is needed.

quiz.q: Define the RMS value of an AC waveform.
quiz.a: The RMS value is the square root of the mean of the squared instantaneous values over one cycle. It equals the DC value that gives the same heating in a resistor.

quiz.q: Why is the full-cycle average of a pure sine wave zero, and what average is quoted instead?
quiz.a: The positive and negative half cycles have equal area with opposite signs, so they cancel. The quoted average is the half-cycle average, 2V<sub>m</sub>/π.

quiz.q: A voltage is v = 200 sin(377t) V. Find its RMS value and frequency.
A heater rated 230 V AC is fed 230 V DC. Does it produce the same power? Explain.
quiz.a: Yes, if its resistance is the same. The 230 V AC rating is RMS, and an RMS voltage gives the same heating as 230 V DC. The AC peak is 325 V, but average power uses RMS.

quiz.q: A coil has N = 100 turns, B = 0.5 T, A = 0.02 m² and rotates at f = 50 Hz. Find its peak emf.
What is angular frequency? Give its relation to frequency and its unit.
quiz.a: Angular frequency is the rate of change of angle in radians per second. It is ω = 2πf, with ω in rad/s and f in Hz.

quiz.q: An AC ammeter reads 5 A on a sine wave. What is the peak current? If the same meter reads 5 A on a distorted wave, is the peak 7.07 A? Explain.
quiz.a: For a sine, I<sub>m</sub> = 5√2 = 7.07 A. On a distorted wave, RMS 5 A does not fix the peak; the shape matters, so the peak is not necessarily 7.07 A.

beyond: Not for the exam. Real generators produce slightly non-sinusoidal voltage because of winding layout and magnetic saturation. Power engineers measure total harmonic distortion to describe this. True-RMS meters compute heating over the actual waveform, not just a sine. Search next for total harmonic distortion, true-RMS measurement and sinusoidal PWM.
